report_name: Researchers Hijack Meta's Muse AI, Access Private Chats

threat_actors.name: NebuSec
threat_actors.description: Security research firm that conducted a proof-of-concept attack against Meta's Muse AI agent to demonstrate architectural weaknesses and responsibly disclosed the findings.
threat_actors.goals: To demonstrate and report on architectural weaknesses in personal AI agent security.

attack_patterns.name: LLM Prompt Injection
attack_patterns.description: A malicious webpage contained a payload that triggered a prompt injection attack, allowing hidden commands to be issued to the Muse agent to exfiltrate its conversation history and memories.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The attack was initiated by luring the Meta Muse AI agent to visit a single malicious webpage, which then triggered the exploit chain.

attack_patterns.name: Escape to Host
attack_patterns.description: A vulnerability in the Muse agent's web browser was chained with a Linux kernel vulnerability to break out of the sandboxed environment and gain control of the underlying host machine.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: After gaining root-level control, the researchers accessed a walled-off credential store containing authentication tokens and passwords for third-party accounts linked to the Muse agent.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The compromised agent was instructed to exfiltrate its own private chat histories and stored 'memories' to an external server.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: A malicious JavaScript payload on a webpage was used to initiate the prompt injection and subsequent exploits against the AI agent.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: The curl utility was mentioned as a command-line pattern, likely used to exfiltrate data from the compromised cloud machine to an external server.

vulnerabilities.name: Muse Prompt Injection Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in the Meta Muse agent that allows for prompt injection attacks from a malicious webpage, leading to hidden command execution and data exfiltration.

vulnerabilities.name: Browser Sandbox Escape Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in the Muse agent's built-in web browser which, when chained with a kernel vulnerability, allows an attacker to escape the sandbox.

vulnerabilities.name: Linux Kernel Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: An unspecified Linux kernel vulnerability that was chained with a browser flaw to achieve a sandbox escape on the cloud machine hosting the Muse agent.

identities.name: Meta
identities.description: Vendor of the Meta Muse personal AI agent, which was the target of the proof-of-concept attack by NebuSec. The company has since patched the disclosed vulnerabilities.

infrastructure.name: Malicious Webpage
infrastructure.description: A webpage crafted by NebuSec to host the initial payload for the prompt injection attack against the Meta Muse agent.

infrastructure.name: Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: An external server controlled by the researchers to receive the exfiltrated chat histories and memories from the compromised Muse agent.

indicators.name: Curl Execution for Data Exfiltration
indicators.pattern:
title: Curl Execution for Data Exfiltration
id: 2b8c1f9a-7e3d-4b1a-9f8c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of curl, potentially for exfiltrating data to a remote server, as seen in the Meta Muse PoC.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-22
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/a-single-malicious-webpage-let.html
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http'
      - '-d'
      - '--data'
      - '-F'
      - '--form'
      - '-T'
      - '--upload-file'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the `curl` command-line tool, which could be used for exfiltrating data to an external server.

indicators.name: Suspicious Proc Filesystem Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Proc Filesystem Access for Evasion
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-2c1d-0e9f8a7b6c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects access to sensitive /proc filesystem entries like /proc/self/environ, which can be used for sandbox escape or environment discovery.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-22
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/a-single-malicious-webpage-let.html
tags:
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.privilege_escalation
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename: '/proc/self/environ'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects access to the /proc/self/environ file, which can be part of a sandbox escape or privilege escalation attempt.

indicators.name: AI Agent Prompt Injection Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: AI Agent Prompt Injection Attempt
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects potential prompt injection attacks against an AI agent by looking for exfiltration commands or keywords in the agent's input logs.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-22
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/a-single-malicious-webpage-let.html
tags:
  - attack.aml.t0051
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
detection:
  selection:
    Prompt|contains|all:
      - 'exfiltrate'
      - 'history'
      - 'credentials'
      - 'ignore previous instructions'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects keywords indicative of a prompt injection attack within logs that capture AI agent inputs, as recommended in the report.
